messages:
alex_support: FYI receiving a high-severity from Acme Analytics — multiple customers seeing 504s and p99 jumps to ~12s on /v1/generate. Ticket C-10234 opened. Posting logs and initial repro.
lina_support: ack. Can you paste a sample request id / cURL they provided? any pattern (large tokens / embeddings)?
alex_support: customer sent this curl and says it was consistently timing out after ~10s for a 1.2k token prompt.
alex_support: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"model":"rw-large-8k","input":"<redacted_prompt>","max_tokens":800}' -v``` 
alex_support: root span shows backend queueing delay: `queue_wait_ms` spikes ~6000ms, `dispatch_latency_ms` ~4000ms. p95 also up from 90ms -> 2.1s in last 20m.
maria_oncall: seeing same. Graphs: region-us-east gpupool-3 shows busy=95% and inflight requests per-worker creeping to 32 (we target 16). admission control is rejecting ~6% of requests (429s) but many still queue and time out upstream.
raj_eng-runtime: interesting — our admission control only checks per-instance concurrency but the router still fans out to warm-but-saturated workers because of sticky routing. possible race with warmup/thundering herd.
sam_sre: can you post the exact timeline? when did p99 start climbing relative to deploys / autoscale events?
alex_support: timeline: 1841120500 small config push to gpupool-3 (kernel tweak) -> 1841120900 minor spike then baseline; spike escalates at 1841122000 and customer reports at 1841122200. No autoscale up events in that window, autoscale-bot shows scale attempts throttled due to capacity limit.
jess_engineering: i can look at the kernel tweak, but short-term mitigations: 1) increase admission control strictness to fail fast (reduce queueing), 2) bump per-worker concurrency lower to avoid tail latency, or 3) route heavy queries to spare pool or fallback model (smaller model/quantized) for customers with SLA.
lina_support: customer wants a short-term rollback if safe — is rollback possible? what risk?
raj_eng-runtime: rollback of kernel tweak is possible but takes ~7-10m to roll across gpupool. Risk: small perf regressions for some short sequences but overall should revert queueing behaviour. Prefer try config toggle: set `queueing_enabled: false` for gpupool-3 to test immediate effect.
sam_sre: quick mitigation we can do now: 1) increase router-level `reject_threshold_ms` from 3000 -> 1200 so requests exceed threshold get 503 immediately (fail-fast) 2) enable per-customer rate-limit for Acme (throttle to 5rps) 3) scale up reserve if tenancy allows.
alex_support: i'm going to ask Acme to accept temporary throttling/redirect to fallback model while we stabilize. Lina will coordinate.
lina_support: pinged customer; they accepted a temporary fallback to `rw-medium-8k-quant` for non-critical pipelines. implementing now.
autoscale-bot: [autoscale] attempted scale-up for gpupool-3: requested +2 nodes; quota limit reached in us-east; pending quota request #Q-778.
jess_engineering: while autoscale is blocked, let's flip admission policy and reduce `worker_concurrency` from 32 -> 16 on gpupool-3; this will reduce throughput but should reduce p99. I'll prepare canary.
raj_eng-runtime: canary patch applied to 2/12 nodes: `worker_concurrency: 16` and `kv_cache_prefetch: true`. Monitoring.
deploy-bot: deploy started by jess_engineering at 1841122500 for gpupool-3 (canary 2 nodes) — rollout strategy: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 2m guardrails.
maria_oncall: after canary (1841122520) p99 dropped from ~12s -> ~3.2s for canary nodes; overall cluster p99 down to ~5.1s. queue_wait_ms for canary nodes under 800ms.
alex_support: customer on fallback reports much better success rate; still some 504s for large batched requests.
sam_sre: next steps — 1) full rollback of kernel tweak if canary improvement holds, 2) increase admission strictness cluster-wide, 3) escalate quota with cloud to permit +3 nodes, 4) add a short-term routing rule: route any request with tokens_requested > 2000 to quantized fallback model.
jess_engineering: agree. i'm scheduling rollback to start in 10m if canary stays stable.
incident-bot: [incident] created INC-2026-11 "gpupool-3 queueing spike" severity=P2; sla impact: sporadic 504s, multiple customers affected.
lina_support: i've updated ticket C-10234 with mitigation steps and asked Acme to keep throttled traffic for 30m — they're ok.
alex_support: leaving notes for customer: we expect full remediation in ~30-45m; will follow up with postmortem.
sam_sre: after action items: - postmortem + perf regression test against kernel tweak - add synthetic load tests with sticky routing to catch fan-out - revisit admission control to support per-pool token-bucket rather than per-instance - expose `queue_wait_ms` in customer-facing dashboard as anomaly signal.
raj_eng-runtime: logging the root cause hypothesis: kernel tweak changed memory allocation pattern causing uneven worker latency, combined with sticky routing + per-instance concurrency allowed per-worker to hit higher tails -> queueing pileup. confirm after rollback.
jess_engineering: thanks all. if canary stays stable i'll promote rollback at 1841122700. will update.
alex_support: thanks team. Lina keep customer in loop. I'll triage next steps with SOC for billing if they request credits.
lina_support: message to customer sent with status + ETA. closing temporary loop once rollback completes.
maria_oncall: final check 1841122790 metrics: gpupool-3 p99 ~2.9s, cluster p99 ~3.1s, queue_wait_ms median down to 120ms. recommending full rollback now.
jess_engineering: rollback executed at 1841122795, monitoring 2m.
incident-bot: [incident] INC-2026-11 update: rollback executed; monitoring for recurrence.
alex_support: marking this thread resolved for support. will attach postmortem link when ready.
